keyVerseText: How he met thee by the way, and smote the hindmost of thee, even all that were feeble behind thee, when thou wast faint and weary; and he feared not God.
rootMeaning: The root of זָנַב (zânab) comes from the primitive root זָנָב (zânâb), which literally means 'tail.' This root conveys the idea of the rear or end part of something, such as an animal's tail or the back portion of a group. The verb form זָנַב, derived denominatively from this root, carries the sense of 'wagging' or more specifically 'cutting off' or 'attacking the tail,' which figuratively extends to striking the rear or the weakest part. This literal sense of the 'tail' as the vulnerable or trailing part adds depth beyond the simple English gloss of 'smite the hindmost,' emphasizing an attack on the vulnerable rear rather than a frontal assault.
usageInScripture: The word זָנַב appears only twice in Scripture, consistently carrying the meaning of attacking or smiting the rear. Both occurrences translate to 'smite the hindmost' or 'smote the hindmost,' highlighting an assault on those lagging behind, often the weak or feeble. This consistent usage underscores the metaphor of pursuing and overcoming the vulnerable or trailing enemies in battle, rather than a general or indiscriminate strike. The limited but focused use emphasizes the strategic and ruthless nature of such an attack in a military context.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding זָנַב enriches our comprehension of biblical warfare imagery and God's dealings with His people and their enemies. The concept of attacking the 'hindmost' reflects the reality of spiritual warfare, where the weak or vulnerable are often targeted, and God's justice ensures protection and vindication for the feeble and oppressed. This term reminds believers of God's sovereignty and care for those who are weak or weary, as well as the certainty that God will confront and judge those who fearlessly oppose Him. It also points to the completeness of God's victory, leaving no part of the enemy untouched, reinforcing the hope of ultimate triumph through Christ.
keyVerseReflection: Deuteronomy 25:18 recounts how an adversary 'smote the hindmost of thee, even all that were feeble behind thee, when thou wast faint and weary; and he feared not God.' The use of זָנַב here vividly portrays an attack on the weakest and most vulnerable members of the community, emphasizing the cruelty and recklessness of the enemy. This word highlights not only the physical vulnerability but also the spiritual danger of neglecting God's protection. It serves as a solemn reminder of the need for God's justice and deliverance for those who are faint and weary, reinforcing the call to trust in God's power to defend and uphold His people.
